keyVerseText: Now on the fourth day was the silver and the gold and the vessels weighed in the house of our God by the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest; and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas; and with them was Jozabad the son of Jeshua, and Noadiah the son of Binnui, Levites;
rootMeaning: The root of בִּנּוּי (Binnûwy) derives from the Hebrew verb בָּנָה (bânâh), which fundamentally means 'to build' or 'to build up.' This root conveys both literal and figurative senses of construction, including establishing a house or family and repairing or setting up something enduring. The noun בִּנּוּי thus carries the sense of something 'built up' or established, emphasizing a foundation or structure that has been carefully and purposefully formed.
usageInScripture: The word בִּנּוּי appears seven times in Scripture, primarily as a proper name referring to individuals associated with the post-exilic community in Israel. It is most commonly translated as 'Binnui,' highlighting its use as a personal name rather than a common noun. The occurrences relate to figures involved in the restoration and reestablishment of Israel, such as a returnee with Zerubbabel and Levites during Ezra's time. This consistency in usage underscores the term's connection to rebuilding and renewal within the community.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בִּנּוּי as 'built up' enriches our grasp of God's redemptive work in Scripture, particularly in the context of restoration after exile. The individuals named Binnui symbolize God's faithfulness in rebuilding His people physically and spiritually. This word reminds believers that God is a God who restores, establishes, and continues His covenant community despite disruption. It points forward to the ultimate building up of the Church through Christ, who is the cornerstone of a spiritual house being built up in faith and holiness.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 8:33 mentions Noadiah, the son of Binnui, among the Levites entrusted with weighing the silver, gold, and sacred vessels in the house of God. The inclusion of Binnui here highlights the ongoing work of rebuilding and organizing the worship life of Israel after exile. The name Binnui, meaning 'built up,' enriches this verse by emphasizing that the community's restoration was not only physical but also spiritual, involving faithful leaders committed to God's service.
